note.text: A twelve-month head start used to buy a company a market. Now the gap between a launch and a credible copy has collapsed to a single quarter, so the real advantage sits in the feedback loop, not the model weights: who ships to the most users fastest, learns from the most failures, and iterates before the next earnings call. Strategy decks built around a defensible technical lead are already obsolete, because the only compounding asset left is organizational speed. Leadership teams still debating a twelve-month roadmap are optimizing for a market that no longer exists.
